Subject: [ALERT] Acme Retail — sudden latency and 5xx spike (us-west)

Lauren,

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx responses and tail latency for Acme Retail (deal ACME-4521) in the us-west cluster at ~07:50 PT. Key points: 
- Error rate jumped from 0.3% -> 3.6% in 15 minutes.
- 95th/99th token latency rose ~2.4x for their production route.
- Throughput to their dedicated pool spiked ~35% due to a batch-arrival pattern change.

I attached a short sampling of error traces and the metrics CSV. Initial look: concurrent KV cache evictions and a small subset of requests triggering a slower model variant (fp16->int8 fallback) which increases per-token time.

Requesting Amber-priority escalation and exec attention — Acme is on a committed SLA. Recommend: immediate war-room, temporary routing to warm fallback pool or pin model variant while we investigate root cause.

Att: error_sample_20280630.log, service-metrics-08-12.csv

—Grace

On Fri, Jun 30, 2028 at 08:36 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> Rishi / Monica: please join an urgent war-room at 08:45 PT.

Quick diagnostic from the infra side:
- Correlated traces show repeated KV cache misses leading to synchronous rebuilds for ~12% of traces. Those rebuilds are hitting the colder int8 execution path because the quantized kernel cache appears to be reporting a miss for a subset of model shards.
- Fallback routing to a higher-latency variant (safer for capacity) triggered when we saw memory pressure on a few nodes. That explains the jump in per-token latency + increased CPU on orchestration agents.

Immediate mitigation I recommend:
1) Switch Acme route to their warm pool (pin to the older fp16 variant) for the next 60 minutes. Owner: infra (me) — I can flip routing at once.
2) Temporarily raise autoscale threshold for the dedicated pool by +20% to absorb bursty arrivals. Owner: infra ops.
3) Enable extended KV cache warming for Acme's prefix set to reduce rebuilds. Owner: runtime team (coord with Grace).

I'll be on the war-room and will perform the route flip now if I get the go-ahead.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Serving Infrastructure

Subject: [AMBER UPDATE] Acme stabilization summary and next steps

Samantha / Priya — thank you for patience and rapid feedback. Brief summary from our war-room: 

What we observed:
- A burst of requests triggered cache churn and a small number of model-variant fallbacks between 07:50–08:20 PT. That pattern caused a temporary increase in token latency and an elevated 5xx rate.

Mitigations executed (completed by 09:30 PT):
- We pinned Acme traffic to the warm fp16 variant for the short term. (Rishi)
- Autoscale threshold for the dedicated pool was raised +20% and additional capacity added to absorb bursty arrivals. (Infra ops)
- Extended KV cache warming enabled for Acme's prefix set; cache rebuilds minimized. (Runtime)

Impact now: error rates have returned to baseline (~0.4%) and 95th/99th latencies are within SLA windows across us-west. We will continue monitoring for 24 hours and will reconvene if any regression appears.

Answers to your asks: 
1) ETA: stabilization confirmed; next formal summary at 24 hours unless you request earlier.
2) Data loss: no evidence of data loss; all requests were processed or retried per our reliability layers.
3) Output fidelity: because routing moved to an fp16 variant (a warmed variant we use in production), outputs are consistent with your configured model behavior. No transformation of content expected beyond minor numeric quantization differences that are within tolerance.

Next steps / tangible owners:
- Postmortem (technical) due EOD tomorrow. Owner: Rishi Malhotra.
- Customer-facing incident report draft and exec note: Monica / Lauren to finalize today.
- Action: implement improved cache warming policy for routes with bursty prefix distributions. Owner: Runtime team (Grace).

If you'd like a 1:1 briefing with our CTO or head of runtime, we can schedule for this afternoon.

Thanks again for quick coordination — we'll keep the channel open.

—Lauren Bishop
VP, Enterprise Sales (acting)
Redwood Inference
